thread:
alex: quick brain dump — I've been sketching a lightweight 'bit negotiator' shim that sits between the route planner and runtime for multimodal models (text+vision). Idea: pick fp8/int8/4bit per-model or per-invocation based on SLO, quality budget, and prompt size. want feedback on interfaces + ops fallout.

maria: sounds promising. main question: is this per-request (slow path) or per-model config negotiated ahead of time?

alex: hybrid. default is per-model profile (fast), but allow per-request overrides when callers provide a quality hint. keeps runtime cheap for common cases.

ben: make sure we can express constraints like "never go below int8 for safety-critical customers". per-tenant overrides need a simple precedence table.

kai: runtime concern: switching mid-request (e.g., for long context where early tokens cheap but later tokens need higher fidelity) is painful. do we intend tokenwise ramping?

alex: optional. prototyping tokenwise hysteresis: ramp up if deg-score exceeds threshold for last N tokens. but default is static per-request.

nisha: ops playbook please — what happens when a new fp8 kernel causes headwise drift? need graceful fallback and fast rollback.

alex: plan = three-layer fallback: 1) per-request fallback to int8 variant, 2) route to compatible model in another scale (small perf hit), 3) degrade to hosted high-SLO path.

ben: telemetry hooks are critical. we need per-invocation: chosen_bitpath, deg_score, surrogate_quality_signal, latency. otherwise we can't debug regressions.

kai: +1. add cohort id and prompt fingerprint to correlate. also think about prefix cache invalidation if we change quantization for a model version.

maria: interface suggestion: a tiny policy proto consumed by planner and runtime. something like:

```
policy {
  model_id: "mosaic-v2"
  default_bitpath: "fp8"
  min_bitpath: "int8"
  overrides: {
    tenant: "enterprise-acme"
    min_bitpath: "int8"
  }
  ramp: {
    enabled: true
    deg_threshold: 0.12
    lookback_tokens: 32
  }
}
```

alex: exactly. keep it serializable and small. runtime uses it to decide kernels and allocate kv-cache formats.

nisha: KV cache format compatibility is big. if we allow mid-flight bit changes, we need a transcoder or versioned cache keys. ops-wise we must avoid rolling back with incompatible caches.

ben: can we restrict mid-flight changes to non-cached flows initially? reduce blast radius.

alex: yes, default: no mid-flight for cached sessions. ramp allowed for stateless short prompts.

kai: bench question: switching between fp8 and int8 changes activation memory and perf. we should model cost savings vs added latency for negotiation. suggest we include a cost_estimate function in planner.

maria: eval plan: shadow traffic with candidate bitpaths, run A/B on quality anchors (QA prompts, hallucination sets, visual-grounding tests). we need thresholds per use-case, not global.

alex: ops-bot FYI — will add a canary that routes 5% of search-calls through fp8 default policy for mosaic-v2 and shadow int8 for QA metric.

ops-bot: deploy-plan created: canary/bit-negotiator/mosaic-v2 -> 5% traffic, shadow int8 logging enabled. Link: https://infra/redwood/canaries/bit-negotiator-1768

nisha: playbook additions: alert on 1) increase in deg_score > 3x baseline, 2) jump in log-loss on eval set, 3) increased tail latency > 10%. automated rollback if any triggers for 3 consecutive minutes.

ben: also a metric for cache-miss-rate when we change bitpath because cache incompat causes perf regressions.

alex: good call. another API question: should callers be able to request "best_quality" or "best_cost"? I think expose quality_hint: [best_quality|balanced|best_cost] and allow tenant policies to override.

maria: yes, but cap overrides for enterprise customers. default hints map to policy bitpaths. keep client ergonomics simple.

kai: edge-case: multimodal adapter layers — vision encoders often saturate in fp8. we need per-module annotations (e.g., encoder=fp16, decoder=fp8) in the policy.

alex: add module_allowlist to proto. runtime will enforce.

nisha: backwards-compat: must gracefully ignore unknown fields so old runtimes don't crash on newer policy. also version the policy proto.

ben: testing: unit tests for planner decision logic + e2e with a smallish dataset that simulates our top 10 customer prompts.

alex: next steps I propose: 1) PR with policy proto and planner stub, 2) runtime adapter that reads proto and emits chosen_bitpath header, 3) canary as ops-bot created, 4) eval harness hook for quality anchors. I'll open issues.

maria: love it. can you add a short RFC follow-up doc listing telemetry keys and the exact fallback order? would help legal/compliance folks.

alex: will do. thanks all. :rocket:

ben: quick note — let's call it 'bit-negotiator' in infra and 'precision-shim' in ML docs to avoid name collision with old 'precision-gateway'. small nit.

alex: ack. I'll standardize naming in the RFC follow-up.

kai: tagging @infra-owners to watch for kernel rollout implications.

nisha: tagging @oncall for the canary window when it goes live.

alex: end of thread — thanks for the quick sync!
